classifiedFinding.title: emergencyTransfer sweeps all funds without zeroing accounting, silently bricking pauseWithdraw

classification.assetImpact: Owner can sweep all phUSD principal and reward tokens; the documented emergency-exit escape hatch (pauseWithdraw) silently reverts afterward because the contract holds zero phUSD. Stakers retain on-chain entitlements against an empty vault.
attackPath: 2. All phUSD and rewardToken balances are swept; contract is paused.
4. Any user attempting pauseWithdraw reverts at the SafeERC20 layer (no balance to send).
classification.likelihood: depends on owner trust; the function is onlyOwner so the trigger is admin action
classification.assumptions: Owner becomes adversarial or compromised; OR honest owner uses emergencyTransfer expecting pauseWithdraw to still work

classifiedFinding.justification: This is an onlyOwner function. Per C4 known-invalid rules, 'Reckless admin mistakes' are out of scope, and pure owner-centralization risks belong in the Centralization (C) bundle. The structural defect (sweep does not zero accounting, breaking the documented escape hatch) is real and worth surfacing, but the trigger is an admin action. Classified as Centralization with strong remediation commentary (restrict sweep to excess balance OR zero per-user state OR add timelock).
classifiedFinding.notes: Sanitizer hinted potential-high. Classifier disagrees: the trigger is owner-only. The defect is real but the gating actor is the trusted admin, which C4 routes to Centralization. The 'silently breaks documented escape hatch' angle is the strong commentary in the C report.
